summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood (AE + SE) and Pegasus Systems (partnership + infra/security leads). Conversation covered integration models (resell vs. joint go-to-market), technical constraints around VPC/private deployments, GPU compatibility, KMS and SOC2 requirements, and a proposed pilot including benchmarking and a technical deep-dive. Agreed next steps include sharing partner assets, scheduling SE deep-dive, and exchanging infra/compliance docs.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Alex Chen, Redwood AE, happy to run through a quick intro on how we typically partner and then hand over to Maya for the tech bits.
[00:00:12] Tom (Pegasus - Head of Partnerships): Thanks Alex, excited to chat. I got Priya (CTO), Samir (cloud infra), and Jules (security) on the line. Quick note, apologies if my audio is a little scratchy.
[00:00:23] Priya (CTO): Yep hi all. We looked at Redwood's site - interesting set of offerings. Curious about dedicated vs hosted, and how the dedicated model fits with our managed GPU fleet.
[00:00:36] Maya (Redwood SE): Hi team. Quick high level: Redwood offers hosted api for fast time-to-value, dedicated reserved capacity for customers who want isolation and predictable throughput, and private deployments for VPC/on-prem. For partners like Pegasus, we see two common models - resell/managed deployments where you operate an instance of Redwood Dedicated on your infra, or a referral/joint go-to-market where your customers consume Redwood hosted but with special routing or co-sell credits.
[00:01:05] Samir (Cloud Infra): Clarifying question - if we run dedicated on our hardware, what parts of the control plane remain with Redwood? Is it a fully customer-managed control plane or a hybrid?
[00:01:18] Maya: Great question. We have a private deployment option where the control plane is customer-managed (you keep keys, network, etc); there is also a hybrid where Redwood manages a lightweight control plane but the inference runtime runs in your VPC. There are tradeoffs on upgrade cadence and monitoring hooks, and we can map those to your operational model.
[00:01:36] Jules (Security): From compliance side, we're primarily concerned about KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and SOC2 scope. Do you have example artifacts?
[00:01:45] Alex: Yes, we'll share SOC2 docs and a KMS integration checklist post-call. Maya, you can add the tech checklist for network requirements.
[00:01:54] Maya: Yep. For KMS we support AWS KMS and bring-your-own-HSM patterns; for private deployments we can integrate customer-managed keys. For audit logs, we emit request-level logs to an S3 bucket or push to your SIEM. There are some retention and PII redaction knobs.
[00:02:12] Priya: Good. Samir, can you talk about our GPU fleet - we have a mix, mostly A100s but a few H100s and some older V100s in edge clusters. We want to avoid fragmentation but also support H100 for specific workloads.
[00:02:28] Samir: Yep. We're running Nvidia A100 80GB, H100, and some older V100. OS is Ubuntu 22.04, drivers vary a bit. We're looking for a partner to help standardize the inference stack and manage quantization/throughput so our customers get consistent latency.
[00:02:41] Maya: That aligns with what we see. Redwood's runtime can pick kernels based on architecture, and we surface model variants and quantization recommendations per workload. One note - sometimes transcriber says "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" - but we do KV cache management to speed up prefix requests.
[00:02:58] Tom: Ha, yes. Also interesting to us is the routing policy you mentioned earlier - like can we route by cost vs latency for different customers?
[00:03:07] Alex: Exactly. Smart routing is a big Redwood differentiator - you can set policies to send latency-sensitive traffic to the fastest pool (e.g., H100 dedicated) and cheaper batch traffic to quantized A100 nodes. For partners, we can expose controls so you can onboard customers with pre-set policies.
[00:03:21] Samir: Network topology question - if we choose the hybrid control plane, do you require VPC peering or private link? What's the recommended pattern for minimal latency and secure comms?
[00:03:33] Maya: We support both VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink patterns. For lowest latency inside a region, peering works well. PrivateLink is better if you want to reduce blast radius; we can provide detailed diagrams. We'll request a list of your VPC CIDRs and peering options during the tech deep-dive.
[00:03:48] Jules: On data residency, some of our customers require EU-only processing - are region pins available?
[00:03:53] Maya: Yes, you can pin deployments and models to regions. For hosted API we have regioned endpoints; for Dedicated/Private you can provision in the region you control. We also have rollout policies for canary and fallback in case of capacity issues.
[00:04:05] Priya: How do you handle fallbacks for model variants? If a user wants a larger model but capacity is tight, what's the degradation path?
[00:04:12] Alex: We surface model variants and automatic fallback rules. Example: primary route -> 70B model on H100, fallback -> 13B quantized on A100 with slightly higher tokenization. You can define SLOs so the system prefers cost or latency. We also have caching to reduce per-token cost for repeated prefixes.
[00:04:30] Tom: From a GTM perspective, we're thinking joint customers who want managed GPU infra and a Redwood inference runtime - we'd like to co-sell and provide a concierge onboarding. Do you have partner program levels?
[00:04:41] Alex: Yes, we have a partner program with tiers: referral, reseller (where you manage billing), and managed service integration. We'll send the one-pager with benefits for each tier. Early partners generally start as referral/joint pilots and then migrate to reseller once there's a track record.
[00:04:57] Samir: Benchmarking - can we run standard perf tests? We want to compare Redwood's runtime on our H100 vs other vendors.
[00:05:05] Maya: Absolutely. We'll run a benchmark harness - typical metrics: p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory footprint. We ask for baseline model weights (or pick from our catalog) and representative prompts. We can run through our CI harness or give you the repo to run locally.
[00:05:21] Priya: Any existing partners running H100 at scale with Redwood?
[00:05:25] Maya: A few partners are on H100; I can anonymize the results. Also keep in mind kernel selection and driver versions can cause TPU-ish differences; ok that's a bad transcribe, but kernel diffs matter.
[00:05:38] Tom: Pricing question - how does dedicated pricing compare to hosted? We need a rough band to present internally.
[00:05:44] Alex: We'll provide pricing bands. Hosted is usage-based per-token with an enterprise discount for committed usage. Dedicated is a reserved capacity model - monthly or annual commitment for GPU pools with options for burst capacity. We'll include an example TCO calc for a typical LLM workload.
[00:05:59] Jules: Security: do you support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and per-route audit logs? Also interested in long-term retention and redaction.
[00:06:09] Maya: Yes - SSO/SAML, RBAC with role mappings, and request-level audit logs as I mentioned. Retention can be configured; we also support automatic PII redaction rules at the ingest layer. For private deployments you can keep logs entirely inside your cloud.
[00:06:23] Samir: For the pilot, can we start with hosted but route some traffic to our dedicated nodes?
[00:06:28] Alex: That's a common hybrid pilot - hosted for lower-friction onboarding, with a canary to your dedicated pool for a subset of traffic. If you want we can instrument tracing and cost breakdowns per token so you can monitor unit economics.
[00:06:41] Priya: About model catalog - do you support fine-tuned variants and private model upload?
[00:06:46] Maya: Yes, private model upload is supported in Dedicated/Private. For hosted we have curated open models and Redwood-verified variants; fine-tunes are supported via model versioning and we can manage rollouts.
[00:06:57] Tom: Anything we should be aware of for resale margins or partner discounts?
[00:07:02] Alex: We'll include partner discount tiers in the partner doc. Resellers usually have a margin ladder based on commit volume.
[00:07:09] Samir: Operationally, how do upgrades work? If Redwood pushes runtime updates, what's the upgrade window and rollback story?
[00:07:17] Maya: For Dedicated we coordinate upgrades - we can do canary nodes and rollback. For private, upgrade cadence is agreed in SLA; customers can choose managed upgrades or self-serve. We'll provide runbooks.
[00:07:28] Jules: On encryption in transit, do you support mTLS between services?
[00:07:31] Maya: Yes, mTLS supported for intra-service comms in the private deployment. Hosted endpoints are TLS with optional client certs for extra security.
[00:07:39] Tom: Ok, sounds promising. Thoughts on timeline - we have a few customers who want pilots in Q1. Is that feasible?
[00:07:45] Alex: Definitely feasible. Typical pilot 6-8 weeks: discovery, infra prep, pilot runs, benchmark analysis. If you want a faster path, start with hosted + burst to dedicated.
[00:07:56] Priya: One more thing - connection with our sales engineering: Samir and I will want a hands-on demo and to run the benchmark ourselves.
[00:08:03] Maya: We'll set up a technical deep-dive. I'll propose times in the Doodle / calendar invite and include a pre-call checklist for network info, SSH access to node images (if you want to run local harness), and sample prompts.
[00:08:18] Alex: Great. I'll follow up with the partner one-pager and pricing, Maya will own the technical follow up. Jules, we'll send SOC2 and KMS checklist.
[00:08:27] Tom: Perfect. Any open questions?
[00:08:30] Priya: No, that's it for me.
[00:08:31] Samir: No, thanks.
[00:08:33] Jules: All good.
[00:08:34] Alex: OK, quick recap: Alex to send partner assets + pricing, Maya to schedule tech deep-dive and bench plan, Pegasus to share infra specs and customer pilot candidates. We'll aim to have the follow-up invites out by Friday. Thanks everyone.
[00:08:51] Tom: Thanks, talk soon.
[00:08:53] [Call ended]
notes: Call included AE+SE from Redwood and partnership/tech/security leads from Pegasus. Good alignment on pilot and partner motion. Recording had a few transcription artifacts (proper nouns and technical terms occasionally mis-transcribed).
